title: Stack a zinc CR2032 coin cell with tweezers and dose its electrolyte by pipette
instruction: Assemble the zinc coin cell in the can that sits in the white mould, using the tweezers for every part: one zinc disc on the floor of the can, then the glass-fibre separator. Then use the pipette, set to 80 uL, to draw electrolyte from the tube and dispense all of it onto the separator (to the first stop; blowing out is optional). Then add the second zinc disc, the steel spacer, the wave spring and the cap, open side down. Every part must lie flat and centred in the can. Press the cap down with your other hand. Put the tweezers and the pipette back in their stands and let go.
context: Battery-materials labs test electrodes in CR2032 coin cells assembled by hand with tweezers. Hand assembly limits throughput and cell-to-cell reproducibility, which is why labs build coin-cell robots (AutoBASS, ODACell), and misaligned electrodes cost capacity and efficiency (NPL GPG 153; DGIST alignment study). Published aqueous-zinc recipe, built in air, ending where labs hand the cell to the crimper.
setup: Both arms empty, grippers open, at the station's ready pose. A white polyethylene-backed absorbent bench pad (400x300 mm) is taped to the table under the work. White POM mould 60x60x20 mm (20.3 mm pocket, 2 mm deep), taped down at x 0.32, y -0.06, holding an MTI CR2032 304SS can (20.0 mm OD, about 19.5 mm inside, 2.9 mm tall; measure and record), open side up. Bergeon 6460 plastic tweezers (119x15x11 mm; tips about 30 mm apart at rest; measure and record), tips down, legs opening along y, in a POM stand 40x40x30 mm with a 37x9 mm slot 25 mm deep, taped down at x 0.28, y 0.02. Two 90 mm glass petri dishes lined with weighing paper on 1 mm silicone, taped down; parts in a row along x, 25 mm apart. Dish A at x 0.32, y -0.17: zinc 12x0.10 mm (x 0.295), Whatman GF/A separator 19x0.26 mm (x 0.32), zinc (x 0.345). Dish B at x 0.22, y -0.13: MTI CR20SPA10 spacer 15.8x1.0 mm (x 0.195), MTI CR20WS-SPR wave spring (about 15 mm OD, 1.2 mm high; measure and record) (x 0.22), MTI CR2032 cap with fitted PP gasket (about 19.3 mm OD across the gasket, about 2 mm tall; measure and record), open side down (x 0.245). Ward's 10-100 uL micropipette set to 80 uL with a fresh 200 uL tip (hook to tip about 185 mm; measure and record), hung by its finger hook in a printed holder at x 0.40, y 0.10: 60x60x8 mm base, post at +x, the 22 mm cradle open towards the robot, set about 203 mm up so the tip hangs about 10 mm clear. 1.5 mL tube with 1.0 mL 2 M ZnSO4 in a POM rack 30x30x25 mm at x 0.24, y -0.22. Phone (4K video) on a clamp arm 45 cm above the mould, inside a diffuse LED ring light. STL files for printed parts provided.
scoring: Procedure (reset notes): overhead 4K video, fingertip blot, 2 kOhm meter cap to can, 0.001 g scale; R0 = max(5 Ohm, 1/5 of the lowest of 3 hand-built cells). Offset: part centre to can axis, in its last frame with the arm away; zinc-to-zinc from those centres. Flat: on the part below, no edge up over 0.5 mm. 1.0: zinc, separator, electrolyte, zinc, spacer, spring, cap (open side down) in order, each once, flat, moved only with tweezers (no finger contact); zincs and zinc-to-zinc max 1.0 mm, spacer 1.5; 0.080-0.120 g; cap pressed, seated; over R0; tools stowed; fingers 3 cm from tools and cell for 1 s. 0.5: same, but zinc 1.0-2.0 mm, spacer 1.5-1.85, 0.050-0.079 or 0.121-0.150 g, a tool out or fingers not clear. 0.25: zinc, separator, electrolyte, zinc, spacer in order, flat, zinc max 2.0 mm, spacer under 1.85, 0.050-0.150 g, over R0; spring or cap missing, inverted, unseated or unpressed. Else 0, incl. wet blot, under R0, electrolyte off the separator, a part lifted back out, a finger contact moving a part over 0.3 mm (cap press exempt).
reset_notes: Scoring method: press a fingertip of each gripper on blot paper (wet = 0). With the cell in the mould and the cap held down by a plastic rod, read cap to can after 5 s. Lift the cell by the can wall with plastic tweezers, cap held, and weigh it: electrolyte = cell minus its dry set. Then take the cell apart (a lab with a crimper may crimp it instead; not scored). Nothing is crimped, so the can, cap, spacer and spring are reused: rinse in water then isopropanol, dry, replace if deformed. Before a session, punch zinc discs (12 mm, from 0.1 mm foil; flatten between glass slides, inspect) and 19 mm GF/A separators (from Whatman 1820-021 21 mm circles) in batches of 20 and keep them flat in a closed dish. New each trial: two zinc discs, a separator (discard stock that sheds fibres), a pipette tip. Weigh each dry set (0.001 g). Refill the tube to 1.0 mL. Wipe spills; dry the pad. Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection: 2 M ZnSO4 irritates eyes and skin. It is toxic to aquatic life: collect used electrolyte, tips, wet separators and wipes as zinc waste for chemical disposal, never down the drain.
fidelity: 480 Hz. Zinc: rigid 0.1 mm discs. GF/A: rigid 0.26 mm disc (real one wets and clings; here zinc can glide). Linings, wave spring: soft contacts. Tweezers: rigid legs, sprung hinge. Can fixed in mould. Liquid is an event: plunger let up with the tip 2 mm under the surface loads 80 uL; pressed with the tip 1-6 mm above the separator, within 3 mm of the axis, adds 0.105 g; else spills. Re-aspiration on let-up not modelled. Sim only: after the cap press, discs may sink into each other. No crimp.
